'''Nawada district''' is one of the thirty-eight [[District#India|districts]] of the Indian [[States and territories of India|state]] of [[Bihar]]. [[Nawada]] is its administrative headquarters. The district is the easternmost district of the [[Magadh division]], one of the nine [[Divisions of Bihar|administrative divisions]] of Bihar. The area of the modern district was historically part of the [[Magadha (Mahajanapada)|Magadha]], [[Shunga Empire|Shunga]] and [[Gupta Empire|Gupta]] empires. [[Koderma district|Koderma]] and [[Giridih district|Giridih]] districts of the state of [[Jharkhand]] lie on the southern border of the district; it also shares borders with the [[Gaya district|Gaya]], [[Nalanda district|Nalanda]], [[Sheikhpura district|Sheikhpura]], and [[Jamui district|Jamui]] districts of Bihar.

==History==

Nawada, located in southern Bihar, has a history deeply connected to ancient [[Magadha]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=District Profile {{!}} District Administration, Nawada {{!}} India |url=https://nawada.nic.in/about-district/district-profile/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |language=en-US}}</ref> Tradition holds that the Magadh Empire was founded here by [[Brihadratha|King Brihadratha]],<ref name=":0" /> and the region was later ruled by major dynasties including the [[Maurya Empire|Mauryas]], [[Gupta Empire|Guptas]], and [[Kanva dynasty|Kanvas]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=History of Nawada |url=https://nawada.biharonline.in/guide/history-of-nawada}}</ref> Archaeological sites, prehistoric rock art, and ancient ruins indicate human settlement for well over a thousand years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nawada Is Full Of Historical Heritage, There Are Many Archaeological Evidences Of This |url=https://www.bhaskar.com/local/bihar/nawada/news/nawada-is-full-of-historical-heritage-there-are-many-archaeological-evidences-of-this-134857896.html}}</ref>

The name “Nawada” comes from the Persian words ''nau-abad'', meaning “new town”. In the colonial era, it was known as ''Eliot Market (Bazaar)''. The ''Khuri River'' runs through the town, with the older part on the left bank and the modern area, including public offices, on the right bank.<ref name=":0" />

During medieval times, Nawada came under the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire, followed by local rulers such as the ''Rajas of Hisua'' and the Muslim [[Mayi (clan)|Mayi clan]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Chatterjee |title=Merchants, Politics, and Society in Early Modern India: Bihar, 1733–1820 |publisher=BRILL Academic Publishers, 1996. |year=1966 |isbn=978-90-04-10303-0}}</ref> Under British rule, it became a subdivision of Gaya district in 1845.<ref name=":0" /> During the 1857 Indian Rebellion, public buildings in Nawada were destroyed, though government records were preserved by hiding them in a nearby hill cave.<ref name=":1" /> On 26 January 1973, Nawada was officially made a separate district.<ref name=":0" />

One of the city’s most important modern landmarks is the '''Sarvodaya Ashram''', inaugurated by India’s first President [[Rajendra Prasad|Dr. Rajendra Prasad]] and later developed by social reformer [[Jayaprakash Narayan]].<ref name=":0" /> It became a hub for socio-political activities in the region.

Nawada is also known for its rich religious and cultural heritage. The ''Surya Narayana Mandir'' at Handiya, believed to date back to the ''Dwaparayuga'' and founded by King [[Jarasandha]], attracts millions of devotees annually.<ref name=":0" /> ''Tapoban'' is regarded as the birthplace of Jarasandha, while ''Sitamarhi'' is associated with the birth of Lava, son of Goddess Sita. The picturesque [[Kakolat Falls]], mentioned in Hindu Pauranic history as the abode of a king transformed into a python by a sage’s curse, is both a popular pilgrimage site and tourist attraction.<ref>{{cite web |title=Destinations |url=http://bstdc.bih.nic.in/Destinations.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706091014/http://bstdc.bih.nic.in/Destinations.htm |archive-date=2015-07-06 |access-date=2015-08-21 |website=[[Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation]] |publisher=[[Government of Bihar]] |at=Eco Circuit |location=[[Patna]]}}</ref> Additionally, Nawada’s location offers easy access to nearby historical cities such as '''Bodhgaya''', '''Pawapuri''', '''Rajgir''', and '''Nalanda.'''

==Geography==
Nawada district occupies an area of {{convert|2494|km2|sqmi}},<ref name='Reference Annual'>{{cite book |editor-last=Srivastava, Dayawanti|title=India 2010: A Reference Annual |chapter=States and Union Territories: Bihar: Government |edition=54th |publisher=Additional Director General, Publications Division, [[Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (India)]], [[Government of India]] |year=2010 |location=New Delhi |pages=1118–1119 |isbn=978-81-230-1617-7|display-editors=etal}}</ref> comparatively equivalent to [[Chile]]'s [[Navarino Island]].<ref name='Islands'>{{cite web |url=http://islands.unep.ch/Tiarea.htm |title=Island Directory Tables: Islands by Land Area |access-date=2011-10-11 |date=1998-02-18 |publisher=[[United Nations Environment Program]] |quote=Navarino Island 2,473 km<sup>2</sup> |archive-date=2018-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180220003634/http://islands.unep.ch/Tiarea.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Most parts of the district are plain but some areas are hilly. The main rivers are the Sakri, Khuri, Panchane, Bhusri by Kakolat and Tilaiya.<ref name="nawada"/>

==Economy==
The main crops harvested in the district are [[Paddy (unmilled rice)|paddy]], [[wheat]], [[pulses]], and vegetables. Industrial facilities in the district include [[Beedi|bidi]] factories and [[silk]] handlooms.<ref name="nawada"/> Formerly, [[sugar cane]] farming and processing also took place; the district's single [[Sugar cane mill|sugar mill]], located in [[Warisaliganj]], is currently non-functional.<ref>{{cite news| title=Five closed sugar mills in state likely to be opened soon| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/Five-closed-sugar-mills-in-state-likely-to-be-opened-soon/articleshow/11371269.cms |work= [[The Times of India]] |date= 5 January 2012}}</ref> Kadirganj, located 6 km from Nawada, has a small scale (Handloom Silk) Industry where more than 100 weavers families involved in weaving handloom silk clothes.<ref name="nawada-district"/>

[[Rajauli]] Hisua and Warsaliganj are emerging as significant market hubs for the hinterland regions bordering [[Jharkhand]] [[States and territories of India|state]], and have also produced many professionals including physicians, surgeons, engineers who are working in many parts of India.<ref name="nawada-district"/> The [[Nuclear Power Corporation of India]] identified Rajauli as the possible site for creating an additional 2,800 MW of nuclear power capacity in the state.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bihar's first Nuclear Power Plant to come up at Rajauli |url=http://news.biharprabha.com/2013/02/bihars-first-nuclear-power-plant-to-come-up-at-rajauli/ |author=BP Staff |publisher=biharprabha.com |date= 4 February 2013}}</ref>

In 2006 the [[Ministry of Panchayati Raj]] named Nawada one of the country's 250 [[Poverty in India|most backward districts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.panchayat.gov.in/brgf-background |title=BRGF Overview |publisher=Ministry of Panchayati Raj |location=New Delhi |access-date=2017-02-07}}{{dead link|date=July 2022|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> It is one of the 38 districts in Bihar currently receiving funds from the [[Backward Regions Grant Fund|Backward Regions Grant Fund Programme]] (BRGF).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.panchayat.gov.in/details-of-brgf-districts |title=BRGF Districts |date=6 June 2014 |publisher=Ministry of Panchayati Raj |location=New Delhi |access-date=2017-02-07}}{{dead link|date=July 2022|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Transport==
[[National Highway 20 (India)|National Highway 20]] runs roughly north–south through the western side of district, serving many villages and towns, including the administrative center of Nawada.<ref>{{cite map |author=ASL Advanced Systems Pvt. Ltd. |title=Road Division Map: District - Nawada |url=http://rcd.bih.nic.in/Maps/Nawada.pdf |publisher=Government of Bihar |location=Patna |format=pdf |access-date=2015-08-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224154954/http://rcd.bih.nic.in/Maps/Nawada.pdf |archive-date=2012-02-24}}</ref> [[National Highway 120 (India)|National Highway 120]] follows a 30 km route in the far northwestern corner of the district, passing through the town of [[Hisua]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rcd.bih.nic.in/Docs/RCD-NH-Road-Statistics-Aug-09.pdf |title=National Highways passing through Bihar |date=2009-08-26 |website=Bihar Road Construction Department |publisher=Government of Bihar |location=Patna |page=3 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224154328/http://rcd.bih.nic.in/Docs/RCD-NH-Road-Statistics-Aug-09.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-02-24 |access-date=2015-08-20 }}</ref> Including [[List of state highways in Bihar|state highways]] and other routes connecting villages, the district has approximately 420 km of paved roads.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rcd.bih.nic.in/Docs/RCD-SH-MDR-Road-Statistics-March-2013.pdf |title=State Highways and Major District Roads across State of Bihar |date=March 2013 |website=Bihar Road Construction Department |publisher=Government of Bihar |location=Patna |page=28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150821233720/http://rcd.bih.nic.in/Docs/RCD-SH-MDR-Road-Statistics-March-2013.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2015-08-21 |access-date=2015-08-21 }}</ref> Deluxe buses are available from Nawada to cities like Patna, Bihar Shariff, Bodh Gaya, Rajgir, Koderma and major cities Patna, Kolkata, Ranchi, Bokaro, Jamshedpur etc.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patna to Nawada Volvo bus service |url=http://www.bus-service.in/patna/nawada-volvo-fare.html |work=bus-service.in}}</ref>

The district lies in the [[East Central Railway zone|East Central Railway]] of [[Indian Railways]]; the [[Gaya–Kiul line]] crosses the district roughly east–west, and connects with the [[Bakhtiyarpur–Tilaiya line]] at [[Tilaiya Junction railway station|Tilaiya Junction]]. Two express trains and several local trains run on the Gaya-Kiul line via [[Nawada railway station]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://indiarailinfo.com/arrivals/nawadah-nwd/1850 |title=Arrivals at Nawada |work=indiarailinfo.com}}</ref> Though electrification is complete, doubling of railway line is under process. This would provide alternative route for Kolkata and North-East bound trains and would enhance passenger services and freight trains. Currently a Delhi bound train is already scheduled and running from Godda to New Delhi and vice versa has halt at [[Nawada railway station]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Arrivals at Nawada |url=http://indiarailinfo.com/arrivals/nawadah-nwd/1850 |work=indiarailinfo.com}}</ref>

S. Census Bureau |access-date=2011-09-30 |quote=New Mexico - 2,059,179 |archive-date=2010-12-27 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20101227010452/http://2010.census.gov/2010census/data/apportionment-pop-text.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>{{why|date=August 2015}} This gives it a ranking of 205th in India (out of a total of [[Districts of India|640]]).<ref name=districtcensus/> The district has a population density of {{convert|889|PD/sqkm|PD/sqmi}}.<ref name=districtcensus/> Its [[Family planning in India|population growth rate]] over the decade 2001-2011 was 22.49%.<ref name=districtcensus/> Nawada had a [[sex ratio]] of 936 [[Women in India|females]] for every 1000 males,<ref name=districtcensus/> and a [[Literacy in India|literacy rate]] of 61.63%. 9.71% of the population lives in urban areas. ==Tourism==
Nawada district has its own tourism splendour and has the potential to develop as a tourist destination. In the town's immediate surroundings, there are various points of interest. The [[Kakolat Falls|Kakolat Waterfall]] (24 km from town), [[Sankat Mochan Mandir Nawada|Sankat Mochan Mandir]]<ref>https://www.livehindustan.com/bihar/story-hindustan-special-this-place-of-bihar-is-amazing-tomb-with-sankatmochan-temple-is-example-of-communal-harmony-8579999.html</ref> and the Sekho Devra Ashram<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shekhodewra Ashram, Kawakole {{!}} District Administration, Nawada {{!}} India |url=https://nawada.nic.in/tourist-place/shekhodewra-ashram-kawakole/ |access-date=2024-08-28 |language=en-US}}</ref> are among them (Sarvodaya Ashram was established here in Kowakole block by Jaiprakash Narayan and inaugurated by Dr. Rajendra Prasad), Baba Majaar and Hanuman Temple (located on NH 31, a shrine of Hazrat Saiyyad Shah Jalaluddin Bukhari and a Hanuman temple), Jarra Baba (found in Sirdalla), Hanuman Mandir (located in Kendua village), and Maa Bageshwari Mandir (located in Kendua village) (located in Jamuawa, in 3 km of Jamui road of Nawada in side of Sakri River).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://nawada.nic.in/tourism/ | title=Tourism | District Administration, Nawada | India }}</ref>

extract: Nawada district is one of the thirty-eight districts of the Indian state of Bihar. Nawada is its administrative headquarters. The district is the easternmost district of the Magadh division, one of the nine administrative divisions of Bihar. The area of the modern district was historically part of the Magadha, Shunga and Gupta empires. Koderma and Giridih districts of the state of Jharkhand lie on the southern border of the district; it also shares borders with the Gaya, Nalanda, Sheikhpura, and Jamui districts of Bihar.
